title: Level 5 (World Class) - C-24
notes:
West leads the ♠4 against 4♠. There are 4 losers (2 each in hearts and clubs) and if South tries to establish the club suit, the defense will be able to take their 4 tricks. Some sort of minor suit squeeze looks to be the only chance, but South cannot afford to rectify the count down to 1 or 2 losers.

If, for example, West's spade opening lead is won with dummy's ♠A, trumps are drawn, and a heart trick is surrendered in an attempt to rectify the count, the denfense will always prevail, almost regardless of the layout of the East-West cards. On the above layout East-West can even cash their other heart trick before leading a club. West's ability to guard the 3rd round of diamonds disrupts any possible squeeze against East regardless of how South plays from this point.

South must hope that a defender with length in both minors was dealt either the ♥A or the ♥K (or both). South will then be able to succeed by running his spades (pitching 1 heart and 3 clubs from the dummy). East will be caught in an unusual 3-suit squeeze that will leave him unable to prevent South from winning a 10th trick.

If East discards the ♥K, South can build a heart trick by knocking out West's ♥A (the ♦K will be an entry to the ♥J). If instead East discards from either minor, South can establish a winner in that suit. The defenders' hearts are blocked leaving them unable to win more than 1 trick in that suit.
